symbols.name: Yspace
symbols.def: Outcome space containing two distinct marked values \(y_-\) and \(y_+\).

symbols.name: yminus
symbols.def: The atom \(y_-\) used only in least-favorable two-outcome submodels.

symbols.name: yplus
symbols.def: The atom \(y_+\neq y_-\) used only in least-favorable two-outcome submodels.

symbols.name: P
symbols.def: A full-data law for \((X,A,Y(0),Y(1))\) inducing the observed record.

symbols.name: fX
symbols.def: The density of \(P_X\) with respect to normalized Lebesgue measure.

symbols.name: betaM
symbols.def: Hölder exponent of the arm outcome laws.

symbols.name: Le
symbols.def: Fixed radius of the propensity Hölder ball.

symbols.name: Lm
symbols.def: Fixed radius of each conditional mean-embedding Hölder ball.

symbols.name: Holder
symbols.def: The periodic isotropic Hölder ball of exponent \(\gamma\), radius \(L\), and values in a Banach space \(\mathbb B\).

symbols.name: H
symbols.def: The tensor RKHS \(\mathcal H=\mathcal H_X\otimes\mathcal H_Y\).

symbols.name: Cbase
symbols.def: The two-outcome feature second-moment operator \(C_{k,b}(P_X)=E_{P_X}[(K_X\otimes b_Y)\otimes(K_X\otimes b_Y)]\).

symbols.name: phi
symbols.def:
The efficient influence function \(\phi_P(O)=\{A/e(X)-(1-A)/(1-e(X))\}\{K_X\otimes L_Y-K_X\otimes
u_A(X)\}+K_X\otimes U(X)-\Psi(P)\), where \(
u_A=A
u_1+(1-A)
u_0\).

symbols.name: mu
symbols.def: The nonzero eigenvalues \((\mu_j(P))_{j\ge1}\) of \(\Sigma_P\), in decreasing order.

symbols.name: thetaPath
symbols.def: The local parameter \(\theta\) indexing a constant-contrast submodel.

symbols.name: epsilonPath
symbols.def: The radius \(\varepsilon_0\) of the local constant-contrast submodel.

symbols.name: Ppath
symbols.def: A one-dimensional local path of full-data laws.

symbols.name: deltaStar
symbols.def: The all-tests minimax separation radius \(\delta_n^\star\) in the unknown-propensity experiment.

symbols.name: deltaStarKnown
symbols.def: The minimax radius \(\delta_{n,e}^\star\) when the realized propensity function is supplied to the test.

symbols.name: partitionH
symbols.def: \(\mathcal B_h=\{B_{h,j}:1\le j\le K_h\}\) is the regular dyadic partition of \(\mathbb T^d\), where \(K_h=h^{-d}\).

symbols.name: chiPair
symbols.def: \(\chi_{n,h,j}=1-(1-p_{h,j})^n-np_{h,j}(1-p_{h,j})^{n-1}\) is the probability that cell \(B_{h,j}\) contains at least two sample covariates.

symbols.name: CgBump
symbols.def: A fixed scale-uniform Hölder regularity constant \(C_g\) for translates and rescalings of the chosen unit-cell bump.

symbols.name: cgBump
symbols.def: The positive squared \(L^2\)-mass \(c_g\) of the chosen unit-cell bump.

symbols.name: Carm
symbols.def: A fixed analytic constant \(C_{\mathrm{arm}}\ge C_g/2\) bounding the \(\mathcal H^{\beta_m}\)-norms of the arm-embedding perturbations generated by the rational cell-probability maps on \([-1/8,1/8]^2\).

symbols.name: gBump
symbols.def: \((g_{h,j})_{j=1}^{K_h}\) are translates and rescalings of one fixed nonzero nonnegative \(C^\infty\) bump supported strictly inside the unit cell, each bounded by one and supported inside \(B_{h,j}\). They have disjoint supports, satisfy \(\|\sum_j\omega_jg_{h,j}\|_{\mathcal H^\gamma}\le C_g h^{-\gamma}\) for \(\gamma\in\{\beta_e,\beta_m\}\), and obey \(\int_{\mathbb T^d}\sum_jg_{h,j}(x)^2\,dx=c_g\).

symbols.name: cFuzzy
symbols.def: The perturbation constant \(c_\circ=\tfrac12[\min\{1/8,1-2\eta,2(L_e-\|1/2\|_{\mathcal H^{\beta_e}})/C_g,(L_m-\|\nu_\star\|_{\mathcal H^{\beta_m}(\mathcal H_Y)})/(C_{\mathrm{arm}}\|b_Y\|_{\mathcal H_Y})\}]_+\), where \([z]_+=\max\{z,0\}\).

symbols.name: PFuzzy
symbols.def: \((P_\omega)_{\omega\in\{-1,1\}^{K_h}}\) is the null-side paired fuzzy family.

symbols.name: QFuzzy
symbols.def: \((Q_\omega)_{\omega\in\{-1,1\}^{K_h}}\) is the alternative-side paired fuzzy family.

symbols.name: GammaOcc
symbols.def: \(\Gamma_n(h;P_X)=\{K_h/\sum_{j=1}^{K_h}\chi_{n,h,j}\}^{1/2}\), with value \(+\infty\) when the denominator is zero.

symbols.name: Mproj
symbols.def: Approximation rank for a higher-order projection.

symbols.name: fuzzyFamily
symbols.def: A paired family of null and alternative Bernoulli likelihoods indexed by local signs.

symbols.name: hoifHandle
symbols.def: The block-local empirical higher-order SCoDiTE correction.

symbols.name: PsiHat
symbols.def: A cross-fitted higher-order estimator of \(\Psi(P)\) produced from the density-adaptive handle.

symbols.name: spectralCriterion
symbols.def: The eigenwise extremal criterion for optimality of a named SKCD statistic.

symbols.name: grid
symbols.def: A geometric grid \(\mathcal G_n\) of regularization levels and correction ranks.

symbols.name: Tgrid
symbols.def: The jointly calibrated maximum of the centered MMD and Wald statistics over \(\mathcal G_n\).

assumptions.condition: The records \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) are independent and identically distributed under \(P\).
\(c_X\le f_X(x)\le C_X\) for Lebesgue-almost every \(x\in\mathbb T^d\).

novel.justification: This maintained Hilbert-valued Hölder condition is satisfied whenever the arm-specific conditional outcome laws vary Hölder-continuously in total variation and the outcome kernel is bounded; it includes conditional location--scale models with Hölder location and scale maps and bounded Lipschitz kernel sections.

assumptions.condition: There exists \(\kappa:\mathbb T^d\to\mathbb R\) such that \(k(x,x')=\kappa(x-x')\).
The kernel mean map \(Q\mapsto\int L_y\,dQ(y)\) is injective on probability laws over \(\mathcal Y\).

definitions.name: modelClass
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M(d,\beta_e,\beta_m,r)=\{P:\ P\text{ satisfies }\mathrm{A}_{\mathrm{cons}},\mathrm{A}_{\mathrm{exch}},\mathrm{A}_{\mathrm{ov}},\mathrm{A}_{f},\mathrm{A}_{e},\mathrm{A}_{\nu},\mathrm{A}_{k,b},\mathrm{A}_{k,c},\mathrm{A}_{k,+},\mathrm{A}_{k,t},\mathrm{A}_{\ell,b},\mathrm{A}_{\ell,c},\mathrm{A}_{\Sigma}\}\), where every displayed index \(d,\beta_e,\beta_m,r\) is fixed.

definitions.name: alternativeClass
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M_1(\delta;s,R)=\{P\in\mathcal M:\|\Psi(P)\|_{\mathcal H}\ge\delta,\ \sum_{j\ge1}\mu_j(P)^{-2s}|\langle\Psi(P),v_j(P)\rangle_{\mathcal H}|^2\le R^2\}\), with indices \(\delta,s,R\) explicit.

definitions.name: deltaStarKnown
definitions.construction: \(\delta_{n,e}^\star\) is defined by the same infimum as \(\delta_n^\star\), with \(e\) supplied as side information to \(\varphi_n\) for every law.

definitions.name: fuzzyFamily
definitions.construction: For any admissible \(P_X\) and dyadic \(h\), use \(\mathcal B_h\), the disjoint supported bumps \(g_{h,j}\), and a uniform sign vector \(\omega\). Put \(u_\omega(x)=a_h\sum_j\omega_jg_{h,j}(x)\) and \(v_\omega(x)=b_h\sum_j\omega_jg_{h,j}(x)\), with \(a_h=c_\circ h^{\beta_e}\) and \(b_h=c_\circ h^{\beta_m}\). For \(u=u_\omega(x)\) and \(v=v_\omega(x)\), the complete conditional cell tables are \[p_\omega=\frac14\begin{array}{c|cc}&Y=y_+&Y=y_-\\\hline A=1&1+u+v+uv&1+u-v-uv\\A=0&1-u+v-uv&1-u-v+uv\end{array},\qquad q_\omega=\frac14\begin{array}{c|cc}&Y=y_+&Y=y_-\\\hline A=1&1+u-v+uv&1+u+v-uv\\A=0&1-u-v-uv&1-u+v+uv\end{array}.\] Equivalently, \(p_\omega(r_A,s_Y\mid x)=(1+r_Au_\omega(x))(1+s_Yv_\omega(x))/4\), whereas \(q_\omega(r_A,s_Y\mid x)=\{1+r_Au_\omega(x)-s_Yv_\omega(x)+r_As_Yu_\omega(x)v_\omega(x)\}/4\). The joint observed-data laws are \(dP_\omega=f_X(x)p_\omega(r_A,s_Y\mid x)\,dx\) and \(dQ_\omega=f_X(x)q_\omega(r_A,s_Y\mid x)\,dx\), extended to full-data laws by drawing \(Y(0)\) and \(Y(1)\) independently from the displayed arm laws given \(X\) and then drawing \(A\) given \(X\). The two fuzzy hypotheses are the uniform mixtures over the shared sign vector \(\omega\).

definitions.name: hoifHandle
definitions.construction: Construct a cross-fitted Hilbert-valued higher-order score from within-cell collision \(U\)-statistics on \(\mathcal B_h\), set \(M=K_h\), stabilize each occupied block by its empirical Gram matrix, and select \(h\) by the candidate bias--fluctuation balance \(h^t+n^{-1}K_h^{1/2}\Gamma_n(h;P_X)\). Couple the upper construction to the corrected paired \(P_\omega,Q_\omega\) family and use the cell-algebra and legality lemmas to keep the exact SCoDiTE null, covariance profile, and source constraint aligned with the lower experiment.

definitions.name: TMMD
definitions.construction: \(T_n^{\mathrm{MMD}}=n\|\widehat\Psi\|_{\mathcal H}^2\), where \(\widehat\Psi\) is the cross-fitted higher-order estimate delivered by the density-adaptive construction.

definitions.name: spectralCriterion
definitions.construction: Diagonalize the joint higher-order score in the eigenbasis \((v_j(P))\), derive for each identity or resolvent filter the exact extremal ratio of source-constrained noncentrality to the sum of null fluctuation, higher-order nuisance remainder, and empirical-operator error, and realize every failing extremal sequence by a legal causal submodel.

definitions.name: Tgrid
definitions.construction: Apply a single cross-fitted multiplier draw to the centered score contributions for every \((\lambda,M)\in\mathcal G_n\), calibrate the maximum by its conditional quantile, and allocate deterministic weights across the geometric grid to obtain an oracle comparison.

definitions.name: rhoOcc
definitions.construction: For dyadic \(h\), set \(K_h=h^{-d}\), \(p_{h,j}=P_X(B_{h,j})\), \(\chi_{n,h,j}=1-(1-p_{h,j})^n-np_{h,j}(1-p_{h,j})^{n-1}\), and \(\Gamma_n(h;P_X)=\{K_h/\sum_{j=1}^{K_h}\chi_{n,h,j}\}^{1/2}\). Define the candidate uniform radius \(\rho_n^{\mathrm{occ}}=n^{-1/2}\vee\sup_{P_X:\,c_X\le f_X\le C_X}\inf_{h\in\{2^{-m}:m\in\mathbb N\}}\{h^t+n^{-1}K_h^{1/2}\Gamma_n(h;P_X)\}\).

statements.statement: Under consistency and conditional exchangeability, \(\Psi(P)=E_P[K_X\otimes\{L_{Y(1)}-L_{Y(0)}\}]\). On the two-outcome submodel supported on \(\{y_-,y_+\}\), this becomes \(\Psi(P)=E_P[K_X\otimes b_Y\{P(Y=y_+\mid A=1,X)-P(Y=y_+\mid A=0,X)\}]\).
statements.justification: This fixes the law-valued causal target while supplying a legal two-outcome reduction for the lower-bound construction.
statements.gap: Jain and Luedtke give the general identifying moment; the embedded two-outcome reduction is needed here to audit exact-null mixtures and source membership without shrinking the ambient model to CATE.
statements.consumer: The reduction makes the least-favorable experiment computable while the resulting frontier continues to govern general conditional outcome laws.

statements.statement: Write the translation-invariant kernel as \(k(x,x')=\sum_{z\in\mathbb Z^d}a_z e^{2\pi i z^\top(x-x')}\), with \(a_z\ge0\). Then \(\Psi(P)=0\) if and only if the \(\mathcal H_Y\)-valued Fourier coefficient \(\widehat{f_XU}(z)\) is zero for every \(z\) with \(a_z>0\). Consequently, over the model class, \(\Psi(P)=0\) is equivalent to equality of the conditional laws of \(Y(1)\) and \(Y(0)\) given \(X\), \(P_X\)-almost surely, if and only if \(a_z>0\) for every \(z\in\mathbb Z^d\); when \(a_0=0\), the constant contrast \(U(x)=b_Y\) is an explicit counterexample.
statements.justification: The minimax null must be the object actually separated by the smoothed embedding, not a stronger verbal homogeneity claim.
statements.gap: Park et al. prove injectivity for the unsmoothed conditional embedding, while Jain and Luedtke invoke a product-kernel argument; neither statement characterizes the centered covariate operator's quotient null.
statements.consumer: Kernel designers can include the constant mode when the empirical claim is conditional-law homogeneity, or report the exact quotient null otherwise.

statements.statement: For every fixed source exponent \(s>0\) and every nondegenerate model class containing a constant-contrast two-outcome submodel with \(a_0>0\), \(\delta_{n,e}^\star\asymp n^{-1/2}\). The upper bound is attained by the bounded oracle estimator \(\widehat\Psi_e\), and the lower bound holds by a one-dimensional regular submodel in the constant Fourier coordinate. Thus covariance eigen-decay cannot improve the worst-case oracle exponent under RKHS-norm separation.
statements.justification: This identifies the correct oracle benchmark before nuisance and spectral effects are compared.
statements.gap: Direct spectral tests obtain nonparametric rates in a stronger \(L^2\)-type separation, while Jain and Luedtke do not state the all-tests RKHS-norm radius.
statements.consumer: It prevents the 401(k) analysis from interpreting whitening as an exponent improvement that the chosen estimand cannot support.

statements.statement: For every \(x\), \(h\), and \(\omega\), write \(u=u_\omega(x)\) and \(v=v_\omega(x)\). The bump normalization and perturbation constant give \(|u|\le a_h\le c_\circ\le1/16\) and \(|v|\le b_h\le c_\circ\le1/16\). The four entries of each table in \(\mathrm{def{:}fuzzy\mbox{-}mixtures}\) sum to one and are at least \(\{1-|u|-|v|-|uv|\}/4>0\). The null table satisfies \(p_\omega=(1+r_Au)(1+s_Yv)/4\), so \(P_\omega(Y=y_+\mid A=1,X=x)=P_\omega(Y=y_+\mid A=0,X=x)=(1+v)/2\) and \(U_{P_\omega}(x)=0\). The alternative table has \(Q_\omega(A=1\mid X=x)=(1+u)/2\) and \[Q_\omega(Y=y_+\mid A=1,X=x)=\frac{1+u-v+uv}{2(1+u)},\qquad Q_\omega(Y=y_+\mid A=0,X=x)=\frac{1-u-v-uv}{2(1-u)},\] whence \[Q_\omega(Y=y_+\mid A=1,X=x)-Q_\omega(Y=y_+\mid A=0,X=x)=\frac{2uv}{1-u^2},\qquad U_{Q_\omega}(x)=\frac{2u_\omega(x)v_\omega(x)}{1-u_\omega(x)^2}b_Y.\] Disjoint bump supports and the shared sign vector give \(u_\omega v_\omega=a_hb_h\sum_jg_{h,j}^2\) and \(u_\omega^2=a_h^2\sum_jg_{h,j}^2\), so \(U_{Q_\omega}\) is independent of \(\omega\), nonnegative in its scalar coefficient, and nonzero. Moreover, for each record cell \(r_A,s_Y,x\), \[2^{-K_h}\sum_\omega p_\omega(r_A,s_Y\mid x)=2^{-K_h}\sum_\omega q_\omega(r_A,s_Y\mid x)=\frac{1+r_As_Ya_hb_h\sum_jg_{h,j}(x)^2}{4}.\] Thus the uniform one-record mixtures coincide exactly. If the constant Fourier weight of \(k\) is \(a_0>0\), then \(\|\Psi(Q_\omega)\|_{\mathcal H}\ge2\sqrt{a_0}c_Xc_ga_hb_h\|b_Y\|_{\mathcal H_Y}>0\).
statements.justification: The displayed cell algebra rules out the erroneous factorization of the alternative and certifies both the exact null and the nonzero SCoDiTE signal before any information bound is invoked.
statements.gap: The scalar fuzzy construction of Kennedy et al. does not record the full SCoDiTE cell table or the kernel-embedded contrast generated by its nonfactorizing alternative.
statements.consumer: The identities provide the auditable null and signal calculations used by every rough-regime lower bound in the proposal.

statements.statement:
Assume the fixed Hölder radii have positive interior slack, so \(c_\circ>0\), and let the nonzero Fourier weights of the fixed periodic kernel, ordered decreasingly, satisfy \(c_kj^{-2r}\le a_{(j)}\le C_kj^{-2r}\), with \(a_0>0\). For every sufficiently small dyadic \(h\), every full-data extension \(P_\omega,Q_\omega\) in \(\mathrm{def{:}fuzzy\mbox{-}mixtures}\) satisfies consistency and exchangeability and has \(\eta\le e_\omega\le1-\eta\). Quantitatively, \(\|e_\omega-1/2\|_{\mathcal H^{ eta_e}}\le C_ga_hh^{- eta_e}/2=C_gc_\circ/2\). Under \(P_\omega\), \(
u_{0,\omega}=
u_{1,\omega}=
u_\star+v_\omega b_Y/2\) and \(\|
u_{a,\omega}-
u_\star\|_{\mathcal H^{ eta_m}(\mathcal H_Y)}\le C_gb_hh^{- eta_m}\|b_Y\|_{\mathcal H_Y}/2\). Under \(Q_\omega\), \[
u_{1,\omega}=
u_\star- rac{v_\omega(1-u_\omega)}{2(1+u_\omega)}b_Y,\qquad 
u_{0,\omega}=
u_\star- rac{v_\omega(1+u_\omega)}{2(1-u_\omega)}b_Y,\] and \(\max_a\|
u_{a,\omega}-
u_\star\|_{\mathcal H^{ eta_m}(\mathcal H_Y)}\le C_{\mathrm{arm}}b_hh^{- eta_m}\|b_Y\|_{\mathcal H_Y}=C_{\mathrm{arm}}c_\circ\|b_Y\|_{\mathcal H_Y}\). Hence the declared overlap and Hölder conditions hold by the definition of \(c_\circ\), rather than by assuming membership of the fuzzy family. There are constants \(0<c_{\mathrm{IF}}<C_{\mathrm{IF}}<\infty\), depending only on the displayed fixed bounds, such that for every component law \[c_{\mathrm{IF}}C_{k,b}(P_X)\preceq\Sigma_{P_\omega},\Sigma_{Q_\omega}\preceq C_{\mathrm{IF}}C_{k,b}(P_X).\] Consequently the density band and the Fourier profile imply \(c_{\mathrm{IF}}c_Xc_k\|b_Y\|_{\mathcal H_Y}^2j^{-2r}\le\mu_j(P_\omega),\mu_j(Q_\omega)\le C_{\mathrm{IF}}C_XC_k\|b_Y\|_{\mathcal H_Y}^2j^{-2r}\); whenever the fixed \(c_\Sigma,C_\Sigma\) bracket these derived constants, all components satisfy the declared covariance profile. For \(0<s\le1/2\), the same lower operator bound and the representation \(\Psi(Q_\omega)=E[K_X\otimes U_{Q_\omega}(X)]\) give \[\sum_{j\ge1}\mu_j(Q_\omega)^{-2s}|\langle\Psi(Q_\omega),v_j(Q_\omega)angle_{\mathcal H}|^2=\|\Sigma_{Q_\omega}^{-s}\Psi(Q_\omega)\|_{\mathcal H}^2\le C_s\|U_{Q_\omega}\|_{L^2(P_X;\mathcal H_Y)}^2\le C_s'a_h^2b_h^2,\] which is at most \(R^2\) for small \(h\). Finally, writing \(\overline P_h^{(n)}=2^{-K_h}\sum_\omega P_\omega^{\otimes n}\) and \(\overline Q_h^{(n)}=2^{-K_h}\sum_\omega Q_\omega^{\otimes n}\), \[\chi^2(\overline Q_h^{(n)},\overline P_h^{(n)})\le\exp\{C n(n-1)a_h^2b_h^2\sum_{j=1}^{K_h}p_{h,j}^2\}-1.\] Under uniform design, \(\sum_jp_{h,j}^2=h^d\); choosing \(h=c_hn^{-2/(2t+d)}\) with a sufficiently small fixed \(c_h>0\) makes the mixture affinity bounded away from zero while \(\|\Psi(Q_\omega)\|_{\mathcal H}\ge c h^t\).
statements.justification: This isolates every model-membership and affinity inequality needed to turn the corrected cell algebra into a legal all-tests lower bound.
statements.gap: Neither scalar CATE lower bounds nor direct kernel tests verify Hilbert arm smoothness, influence-covariance stability, and covariance-dependent source membership for the same exact-null causal mixture.
statements.consumer: The lemma makes the nuisance lower theorem reusable and gives the arbitrary-density question a concrete construction whose remaining difficulty is the occupancy match, not basic legality.

statements.statement: Suppose \(0<s\le1/2\), \(t<d/2\), the Hölder balls contain the balanced two-outcome baseline in their interiors, and the fixed periodic kernel has \(a_0>0\) and ordered nonzero Fourier weights \(a_{(j)}\asymp j^{-2r}\), with the declared covariance-profile constants wide enough to contain the derived sandwich in \(\mathrm{lem{:}fuzzy\mbox{-}legality\mbox{-}affinity}\). Under uniform \(P_X\), \(\delta_n^\star\ge c n^{-2t/(2t+d)}\) for a class constant \(c>0\). At \(h=c_hn^{-2/(2t+d)}\), every \(P_\omega\) belongs to \(\mathcal M_0\), every \(Q_\omega\) belongs to \(\mathcal M_1(cn^{-2t/(2t+d)};s,R)\), the one-record mixtures coincide exactly, and the \(n\)-record mixtures have affinity bounded away from zero. Hence \(\delta_n^\star/\delta_{n,e}^\star\to\infty\).
statements.justification: This is an all-tests information bound, so it survives arbitrary higher-order correction and establishes a genuine nuisance cost.
statements.gap: Kennedy et al. provide a scalar CATE fuzzy bound; the exact Hilbert null, embedded signal, and covariance-source constraint are new here.
statements.consumer: It tells analysts when no regularization or nuisance learner can restore oracle sensitivity in observational conditional-distribution testing.

statements.statement: If \(t>d/2\), then over every law in \(\mathcal M\) and every design density satisfying \(c_X\le f_X\le C_X\), a finite-order cross-fitted empirical higher-order SCoDiTE test has uniform type-I error at most \(\alpha+o(1)\) and uniform type-II error at most \(\beta+o(1)\) whenever \(\|\Psi(P)\|_{\mathcal H}\ge Cn^{-1/2}\). Thus \(\delta_n^\star\le Cn^{-1/2}\); this upper bound uses only the declared model assumptions, its correction has \(M=o(n)\), and it imposes no smoothness on \(f_X\). For the reverse inequality only, impose the class-richness premise that \(\mathcal M\) contains a path \((P_\theta)_{|\theta|\le\varepsilon_0}\) supported on \(\{y_-,y_+\}\), with \(P_0\in\mathcal M_0\), fixed \(P_X\) and \(e\), constant contrast \(U_{P_\theta}(x)=\theta b_Y\), nonzero derivative \(w_0=E_{P_0}[K_X]\otimes b_Y\), quadratic-mean differentiability at zero with Fisher information strictly between zero and infinity, and \(\sup_{|\theta|\le\varepsilon_0}\sum_{j\ge1}\mu_j(P_\theta)^{-2s}|\langle w_0,v_j(P_\theta)\rangle_{\mathcal H}|^2<\infty\). Under this premise, the local two-point reduction gives \(\delta_n^\star\ge cn^{-1/2}\), and hence \(\delta_n^\star\asymp n^{-1/2}\).
statements.justification: The high-smoothness upper bound isolates density-robust higher-order correction, while the explicitly conditional local-path reduction supplies only the ordinary parametric lower bound and is not the nuisance-rate crux.
statements.gap: Liu, Mukherjee, Newey, and Robins prove semiparametric efficiency for the scalar mean under missing at random and a broader scalar doubly robust class using an empirical Gram basis of dimension \(k=o(n)\); they do not prove a Hilbert-valued testing expansion or uniform exact-null calibration.
statements.consumer: It supplies a primitive size guarantee for SCoDiTE applications with nonuniform covariates whenever total nuisance smoothness is above the elbow, and states exactly when that upper rate is also a minimax equality.

statements.statement: Flagship question: for fixed \(r>1/2\), \(s>0\), and \(0<t\le d/2\), prove or refute the candidate equivalence \(\delta_n^\star\asymp\rho_n^{\mathrm{occ}}\) uniformly over \(c_X\le f_X\le C_X\), where \(\rho_n^{\mathrm{occ}}\) is defined from the primitive cell probabilities, pair-occupancy probabilities, and Gram-inflation factor in \(\mathrm{def{:}occupancy\mbox{-}gram\mbox{-}candidate}\). The lower-bound route must use the explicit nonfactorizing \(q_\omega\) table and shared-sign family \(\{P_\omega,Q_\omega:\omega\in\{-1,1\}^{K_h}\}\) from \(\mathrm{def{:}fuzzy\mbox{-}mixtures}\) at the optimizing scale. Its named obligations are to preserve the exact \(U_{P_\omega}=0\) SCoDiTE null, the nonzero contrast \(U_{Q_\omega}=2u_\omega v_\omega b_Y/(1-u_\omega^2)\), the covariance sandwich and \(0<s\le1/2\) source bound from \(\mathrm{lem{:}fuzzy\mbox{-}legality\mbox{-}affinity}\), and bounded \(n\)-record mixture affinity at the scale selected by the nonuniform cell probabilities. The upper-bound route must either attain this candidate by collision and empirical-Gram calibration or replace it with a rigorously derived primitive occupancy--Gram functional and match that radius. For \(s>1/2\), determine whether covariance-source membership eliminates this fuzzy branch or yields an explicit \((r,s)\)-dependent frontier.
statements.justification: This flagship claim turns the rough arbitrary-density bottleneck into a falsifiable rate formula and exposes exact-null legality and covariance-source membership as independent proof obligations.
statements.gap: Liu et al. prove their empirical-HOIF efficiency result for scalar missing-at-random and doubly robust functionals with \(k=o(n)\); scales with \(K_h>n\) are therefore not subsumed, but that fact alone neither proves an obstruction nor selects the proposed occupancy factor. No SCoDiTE result supplies the missing lower and upper match.
statements.consumer: The matched frontier determines the size-valid detection threshold for the 401(k) conditional wealth-distribution analysis and tells the analyst whether cell occupancy, rather than a heuristic whitening rule, limits sensitivity.

statements.statement: Conditional on the radius delivered by \(\mathrm{oeq{:}arbitrary\mbox{-}density\mbox{-}frontier}\), derive a necessary-and-sufficient spectral criterion for \(T_n^{\mathrm{MMD}}\) and for some \(T_{n,\lambda_n}^{\mathrm{Wald}}\) to attain \(\delta_n^\star\) at each covariance exponent \(r\) and source exponent \(s\). The criterion must be an explicit eigenwise extremal ratio incorporating source-constrained signal, null effective dimension, higher-order nuisance remainder, and empirical-operator error; failure in either named statistic must be witnessed by a legal sequence in \(\mathcal M_1\).
statements.justification: A method comparison is meaningful only after the all-tests modulus and nuisance amplification are in the same sequence experiment.
statements.gap: Hagrass et al. classify direct two-sample filters under a different loss, while Jain and Luedtke analyze fixed regularization without an iff minimax criterion.
statements.consumer: The criterion tells the 401(k) analyst when covariance whitening improves local power, when it only changes constants, and when it loses to identity weighting.

statements.statement: Construct \(T_n^{\mathrm{grid}}\) over a grid of at most \(C\log n\) regularization--rank pairs with uniform asymptotic level \(\alpha\). Prove an oracle inequality attaining every radius certified by \(\mathrm{oeq{:}spectral\mbox{-}iff}\) up to an explicit logarithmic or iterated-logarithmic factor, and prove by a multi-scale mixture that no jointly adaptive test can remove that factor over the declared compact index ranges.
statements.justification: The practical statistic must choose both how much to whiten and how much higher-order correction to apply without invalidating size.
statements.gap: Direct MMDAgg and spectral aggregation use exchangeable raw samples; Jain and Luedtke leave data-driven Wald regularization open and calibrate only a fixed operator.
statements.consumer: This replaces the heuristic Wald regularizer in the 401(k) analysis by a size-valid, data-adaptive choice.

sampling_model.design: Independent observational sampling from a full-data law with consistency and conditional exchangeability.
sampling_model.units: \(n\) independent units with \(X\in\mathbb T^d\), binary treatment, and outcomes in the standard Borel space \(\mathcal Y\); two-outcome laws are used only as least-favorable submodels.
sampling_model.treatment: Unknown Hölder propensity \(e\) with fixed overlap; a comparison experiment supplies \(e\) to the test.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Cross-fitted propensity and arm-law estimation, followed by a block-local empirical higher-order correction and, for Wald statistics, a cross-fitted covariance estimate.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The paper gives a test with valid type 1 error and consistency against fixed alternatives.
The minimax lower bound is attained by a local polynomial R-Learner under additional design-density conditions.

Version 5 proves semiparametric efficiency without covariate-density smoothness for the scalar mean under missing at random, and extends the construction to a class of scalar doubly robust functionals, using an empirical Gram basis with \(k=o(n)\).
Spectral regularization is minimax optimal with a smaller separation boundary than MMD in direct two-sample testing.
A moderated kernel test attains source-class goodness-of-fit rates that ordinary MMD can miss.
MMDAgg is minimax adaptive over Sobolev balls up to an iterated logarithmic term.
Cross-fitted one-step estimators can be efficient for differentiable Hilbert-valued parameters.
A characteristic outcome kernel makes the unsmoothed pointwise conditional discrepancy identify equality of conditional laws.
Random design changes the minimax rate for nonparametric variance estimation.
Occupancy-aware binning attains minimax conditional-independence testing rates under smooth conditional laws.

tldr: The flagship question is whether the all-tests SCoDiTE separation radius under an arbitrary covariate density bounded above and below equals the explicit candidate \(\rho_n^{\mathrm{occ}}\), which balances Hölder bias against a pair-occupancy and empirical-Gram inflation functional built from primitive cell probabilities. The converse is anchored by full \(2\times2\) Bernoulli cell tables: the null law factorizes and has \(U=0\), while the alternative does not factorize and has \(U_\omega=2u_\omega v_\omega b_Y/(1-u_\omega^2)\neq0\). Shared signs and disjoint bump supports make the one-record mixtures identical, while explicit Hölder, overlap, covariance-sandwich, source-norm, signal, and \(n\)-mixture bounds yield the slower uniform-design radius \(n^{-2(\beta_e+\beta_m)/(2(\beta_e+\beta_m)+d)}\) for \(0<s\le1/2\) below the smoothness elbow. Under its stated nondegeneracy condition, the known-propensity experiment has a root-\(n\) RKHS-norm boundary. Above the elbow, the declared assumptions deliver a density-robust root-\(n\) upper bound; the matching lower bound requires only the separately stated regular constant-contrast path. Once the arbitrary-density modulus is settled, an eigenwise iff criterion compares higher-order SKCD--MMD with regularized SKCD--Wald, and a jointly calibrated grid selects regularization and correction rank. Characteristicness of the outcome kernel does not by itself convert the covariate-smoothed moment null into pointwise conditional homogeneity.

project_justification.gap: Existing SCoDiTE theory is first order and pointwise in the law, direct spectral tests omit causal nuisances, and the empirical-HOIF theorem of Liu et al. treats scalar missing-at-random and doubly robust functionals with \(k=o(n)\). It therefore does not settle rough SCoDiTE scales with \(K_h>n\), although that non-subsumption alone is not evidence that occupancy worsens the rate.
project_justification.niche: The unoccupied flagship object is the all-tests separation modulus for a Hilbert-valued causal moment under only a positive bounded design density, expressed through a falsifiable primitive occupancy--Gram candidate and matched by legal exact-null causal experiments.
project_justification.fill: The candidate \(\rho_n^{\mathrm{occ}}\) records cell-pair availability and empirical-Gram inflation. The displayed \(P_\omega,Q_\omega\) tables separate a factorizing exact-null law from a nonfactorizing alternative with \(U_\omega=2u_\omega v_\omega b_Y/(1-u_\omega^2)\), and the legality lemma derives positivity, overlap, both Hölder memberships, nonzero \(\Psi\), covariance stability, the \(0<s\le1/2\) source bound, and mixture affinity from the construction. A collision-based higher-order score supplies the arbitrary-density attainment handle, and the resulting modulus feeds the spectral iff and adaptive-grid questions. In the high-smoothness branch the score yields the root-\(n\) upper bound under the declared assumptions, while equality uses a separately stated nondegenerate constant-contrast path only for the local lower-bound reduction.

related_work: Jain and Luedtke (2026) define the SCoDiTE moment, its efficient Hilbert influence function, and fixed-operator MMD and Wald tests; their product-rate theorem and fixed-alternative consistency supply the starting experiment. Their local asymptotic theory also motivates the ordinary root-\(n\) lower-bound reduction, which here is invoked only under an explicit nondegenerate quadratic-mean differentiable constant-contrast path inside the declared class. Park, Shalit, Schölkopf, and Muandet (2021) study an unsmoothed pointwise conditional embedding discrepancy; that result motivates comparison but does not justify the maintained Hilbert-valued periodic Hölder condition and does not identify the quotient null after covariate smoothing. Kennedy, Balakrishnan, Robins, and Wasserman (2024) supply the localized fuzzy-hypothesis architecture, but the present paired construction requires a different nonfactorizing alternative cell table so that the null has \(U=0\) and the alternative has the explicit nonzero Hilbert contrast. Liu, Mukherjee, Newey, and Robins (2026, arXiv:1705.07577v5) prove semiparametric efficiency without density smoothness for a scalar missing-at-random mean and a class of scalar doubly robust functionals using empirical Gram bases with \(k=o(n)\); this informs the upper-bound handle but does not cover Hilbert testing or \(K_h>n\). Hagrass, Sriperumbudur, and Li (2024) and Balasubramanian, Li, and Yuan (2021) supply direct-sample spectral extremal arguments under a different separation metric. Schrab et al. (2023) supply the dependent-grid calibration template. Shen, Gao, Witten, and Han (2020) and Neykov, Balakrishnan, and Wasserman (2021) show in adjacent random-design problems that occupancy can enter minimax rates and test construction. None of these papers states the candidate occupancy--Gram SCoDiTE frontier or jointly supplies the exact-null cell algebra, covariance sandwich, source bound, and mixture-affinity calculation used here.
technical_internal_limitation: For the early kill case \(d=1\), \(\beta_e=\beta_m=0.2\), the uniform-design benchmark is \(n^{-4/9}\) and its nominal partition size is \(K_h\asymp n^{10/9}>n\). This lies outside Liu et al.'s proved \(k=o(n)\) empirical-HOIF regime and establishes non-subsumption only. The corrected fuzzy construction settles the componentwise cell algebra: \(p_\omega\) factorizes, \(q_\omega\) does not, and their shared-sign one-record mixtures agree. The remaining early-kill audit is the upper procedure over the full density band and the match between its empirical-Gram fluctuation and \(\Gamma_n(h;P_X)\); failure requires replacing the candidate primitive functional. The rough lower theorem also requires interior Hölder radii and a fixed kernel whose Fourier profile yields the declared covariance constants, while the model in general permits kernels without a constant Fourier mode. The two-outcome family is a proof device inside the general outcome-law model; an attaining procedure must still handle the multivariate wealth outcome in the 401(k) illustration.
honest_scope: The known-propensity root-\(n\) benchmark, the corrected rough uniform-design lower branch, the high-smoothness empirical-HOIF upper branch, and the Fourier quotient-null theorem are posed for proof. The rough lower branch explicitly derives the exact null, nonzero alternative, overlap, propensity and arm-embedding Hölder bounds, covariance eigen-profile stability, the \(0<s\le1/2\) source norm, and bounded mixture affinity; it is conditional only on positive radius slack and a fixed kernel with the stated Fourier profile, not on assumed fuzzy-family membership. In the high-smoothness branch, the matching root-\(n\) lower bound and thus the two-sided minimax equality are conditional on the explicitly stated class-richness premise. The flagship answer-open content is the rough arbitrary-density equivalence with the candidate occupancy--Gram radius; the candidate may be refuted and replaced by a matched primitive functional. The spectral iff classification and adaptive grid calibration remain downstream open questions. No claim is made that \(K_h>n\) itself proves an occupancy penalty, or that characteristic constituent kernels automatically make the smoothed null identical to conditional homogeneity. Under \(e\equiv1/2\), uniform \(P_X\), and a nonzero constant low-frequency contrast, the construction reduces to bounded Hilbert-mean testing with root-\(n\) separation.

novelty_justification: The closest causal result is Jain and Luedtke's first-order SCoDiTE theory; the closest smooth causal frontier is Kennedy et al.'s scalar CATE theorem; and the closest arbitrary-density higher-order method is Liu et al.'s arXiv:1705.07577v5 empirical-HOIF construction for scalar missing-at-random and doubly robust functionals with \(k=o(n)\). The flagship object is the arbitrary-design all-tests radius for the kernel-specific SCoDiTE norm. It tests the explicit candidate \(\rho_n^{\mathrm{occ}}\), in which \(\chi_{n,h,j}\) measures primitive pair occupancy and \(\Gamma_n(h;P_X)\) measures the resulting block-Gram inflation. The converse uses fully displayed conditional masses: \(p_\omega=(1+r_Au_\omega)(1+s_Yv_\omega)/4\) has \(U=0\), whereas \(q_\omega=(1+r_Au_\omega-s_Yv_\omega+r_As_Yu_\omega v_\omega)/4\) is nonfactorizing and yields \(U_\omega=2u_\omega v_\omega b_Y/(1-u_\omega^2)\neq0\). Disjoint supports and shared signs give exact equality of the uniform one-record mixtures. Separate quantitative bounds derive positivity, overlap, propensity and arm-embedding Hölder membership, nonzero \(\Psi\), a covariance-operator sandwich and polynomial eigen-profile, the \(0<s\le1/2\) source norm, and bounded \(n\)-record affinity at \(h\asymp n^{-2/(2t+d)}\); none of these memberships is assumed. The fact that the rough optimizer can have \(K_h>n\) only shows that Liu et al. do not subsume the question; it is not evidence that the candidate penalty is correct. The high-smoothness upper theorem is stated over the declared model without an implicit submodel assumption, and its matching parametric lower bound is separated behind an explicit regular constant-contrast richness premise. The Fourier quotient-null theorem prevents characteristicness from being invoked after covariate smoothing without full covariate spectral support.
